title: 5 Signs Your Website Needs a Redesign
excerpt: Your website might be costing you customers without you knowing. Here are the warning signs — and what to do about them.

content.text: Your website is your most important marketing asset. But many businesses are running on outdated, underperforming sites that actively drive customers away.
Here are five signs your website needs a redesign — and what to do about it.
Over 70% of Kenyan web traffic comes from mobile devices. If your site isn't optimized for mobile, you're losing the majority of your potential customers.
Test it: pull up your site on your phone. Can you read the text without zooming? Is the navigation easy to use? Do buttons work with your thumb?
Google says 53% of mobile users abandon sites that take more than 3 seconds to load. If your site is slow, you're losing over half your visitors before they see your content.
Test it: use Google PageSpeed Insights. Anything below 70/100 needs attention.
A website that looks good but doesn't generate enquiries is an expensive business card. If visitors aren't converting into leads, the site isn't doing its job.
Average website conversion rate is 2-3%. If yours is below 1%, something is fundamentally broken — usually the design, copy, or user flow.
Sign 4: Your Brand Has Outgrown It
If your brand has evolved but your website hasn't, there's a disconnect. Customers judge consistency. A dated website undermines a modern brand.
Sign 5: You're Embarrassed to Share It
This one's simple: if you don't want to send people to your website, it needs a redesign. Your website should be something you're proud to share.
A proper redesign isn't just cosmetic. It includes:

items: Strategy: Understanding your audience and goals
SEO: Preserving and improving your search rankings

content.text: "We knew our site needed work, but we didn't realize how much business we were losing until we redesigned. Enquiries doubled in the first month." — Director, Nairobi architecture firm
